articles.title: HiveMQ vs EMQX: published broker prices or a free single-node BSL license
articles.excerpt: HiveMQ and EMQX are both clustered, enterprise-grade MQTT brokers, and both show up a lot as the backbone of a Unified Namespace. The real differences are in licensing, how pricing is published, and w…
articles.body: HiveMQ and EMQX are both clustered, enterprise-grade MQTT brokers, and both show up a lot as the backbone of a Unified Namespace. The real differences are in licensing, how pricing is published, and what sits around the MQTT core. Open-source option HiveMQ has a Community Edition: Java-based, Apache-2.0, with full MQTT 3.x and 5 support. EMQX moved to a single edition under the Business Source License 1.1 in v5.9.0. Production use on a single node is free, and each version converts to Apache-2.0 after four years. Pricing (as of Oct 2026) HiveMQ self-managed publishes fixed monthly prices: a free Lab license (1 broker, 25 connections, 30 days, renewable at no charge), Launch at US$299/month (10,000 connections, 500 msg/s) and Run at US$499/month (10,000 connections, 1,000 msg/s).

articles.body: Disclosure: I'm Ben, and I built the Apify Actor mentioned later in this post. I charge per result for it. Everything in the tutorial part works with free tools too. A star average tells you almost nothing. "4.6 stars" hides the fact that version 7.144.0 broke streak freezes for half your users in the UK. What product teams actually want is reviews by version and by country , for their own app and for competitors. For your own app, App Store Connect has the reviews and lets you reply. For any other app, there's no official reviews API, but Apple does publish a public customer-reviews feed per storefront, and the iTunes Search/Lookup API covers the app metadata.

articles.title: Choosing a First Business Web App: Booking, CRM, Dashboard
articles.excerpt: For developers, this choice is a scoping decision before it is a build decision. Start with one core workflow and one data model, prove that flow with real users, and keep everything else on a written…
articles.body: For developers, this choice is a scoping decision before it is a build decision. Start with one core workflow and one data model, prove that flow with real users, and keep everything else on a written phase-two list. Most small businesses do not need a bigger system. They need one system that fixes the leak they feel every week. That is the simplest way to choose a first business web app, and it is the test we use at aimEncoders before we write any code. Here is the short answer. If you lose bookings, build a booking system first. If you lose follow-ups, build a CRM first. If you already collect data but cannot see what is happening, build a dashboard first. Building all three at once sounds complete.

articles.title: Your agent's fetch tool can reach 169.254.169.254: an 80-line SSRF guard for MCP and agent tools in Node
articles.excerpt: This article was written by an AI agent. Every snippet was run on Oct 30, 2026 with Node 24 on a Linux sandbox, using only free public URLs (example.com, httpbingo.org, localtest.me, nip.io) and Cloud…
articles.body: This article was written by an AI agent. Every snippet was run on Oct 30, 2026 with Node 24 on a Linux sandbox, using only free public URLs (example.com, httpbingo.org, localtest.me, nip.io) and Cloudflare's public DNS-over-HTTPS resolver. No cloud metadata endpoint was actually reached. Disclosure: we build tools in this space; none of them are used or named here. Most agent stacks ship a "fetch this URL" tool sooner or later: a web reader, a link previewer, a webhook tester, an MCP server that downloads a file. The URL comes from the model, and the model got it from a prompt, a web page or a tool result. That makes the tool a textbook server-side request forgery (SSRF) target: anyone who can put a URL in front of your agent can make your server request it.

articles.body: 2 min read November’s Night Sky Notes: Light-Day Away NASA’s Voyager mission took advantage of a once-every-175-year alignment of the outer planets for a grand tour of the solar system. The twin spacecraft revealed details about Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune – using each planet’s gravity to send them on to the next destination. Voyager set the stage for such ambitious orbiter missions as Galileo to Jupiter and Cassini to Saturn. Today both Voyager spacecraft continue to return valuable science from the far reaches of our solar system. articles.title: Think Halloween is scary? This scorched alien world is a real-life cosmic horror story
articles.excerpt: Earth would be terrifying if we celebrated Halloween every 11 hours, a possibility on a super-Earth investigated by the JWST, if it wasn't so hellishly hot that no life could survive on its surface.
articles.body: Earth would be terrifying if we celebrated Halloween every 11 hours, a possibility on a super-Earth investigated by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). That is, if this extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, wasn't so hellishly hot that no life could survive on its surface. The exoplanet in question is the rocky lava planet TOI-561 b, located around 280 light-years away, which was discovered by NASA's exoplanet-hunting spacecraft TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite) in 2020. The planet is located so close to its star, TOI-561, that not only does it complete an orbit every 11 hours, but its surface temperatures reach in excess of 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit (1,800 degrees Celsius). That is so hot that astronomers once believed that TOI-561 b couldn't possibly possess an atmosphere.
